newsitem.title: UK: NWE spot gasoline prices slump as supports give wa.
newsitem.headline: NWE spot gasoline prices slump as supports give wa.

text.p: NWE spot gasoline prices slumped on Tuesday as support from strike-related short covering and transatlantic arbitrage offtake gave way, traders said.
Spot prices for Eurograde gasoline barges have dropped by around $10-12 a tonne since last Friday with European demand muted and high freight costs tightening arbitrage profitablity.
"The arbitrage still works on paper but expensive freight costs are making it very tight," one trader said.

Traders said the combination of an end to the last week's Elf refinery strike and weaker U.S. markets had tipped the balance in Europe, but said today's one day strike at some French refiners may still have some repurcussions.

The end to the strike loosened the grip on a tigher gasoline market on Monday traders said, but an open arbitrage to the U.S. and heavy buying by Elf to make up for its production cuts had help underpin gasoline prices.
"The market's not that oversupplied on the prompt side and any short covereing against today's strikes could give some short term support," one trader said.

NYMEX gasoline futures gave up over 1.5 cents a gallon and New York harbour cash prices fell sharply. Traders said this was as a result of the effects of November imports of around 650,000 tonnes which have started to hit the Gulf Coast market.
